documents.title: Un-Audited Financial Results For The Quarter Ended 30Th June, 2026
Board Meeting Outcome for Outcome Of Board Meeting Held On 7Th August, 2026
Board Meeting Intimation for Consideration And Approval Of The Un-Audited Financial Results For The Quarter Ended 30Th June, 2026
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: For the financial year 2024-25, Pasupati Acrylon Limited achieved revenue from operations of Rs. 62,143.18 Lakh and a profit after tax of Rs. 3,538.12 Lakh. The company successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant in March 2025 with an expenditure of approximately Rs. 188 Crore.

guidance.claim: The company expects to commence commercial production of its grain-based Ethanol Project by September 2024.
guidance.quote: Further, the Company has already initiated steps to establish grain based Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD and it is expected to commence commercial production of Ethanol by September, 2024.

guidance.claim: The company expects sales and production to improve further in coming years while monitoring cost factors like inflation and energy prices.
guidance.quote: The sale and production has seen good improvement from previous year and it is expected to improve more in the coming years but it is necessary to carefully watch other factors such as inflation, high energy prices etc.

demand_outlook.claim: Pasupati Acrylon anticipates sustained demand growth across its business segments.
demand_outlook.quote: Your Company anticipates sustained demand growth across segments.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for acrylic fibers is expected to rise due to macroeconomic development in end-use sectors.
demand_outlook.quote: The demand for acrylic fibers is anticipated to rise in the coming years, particularly due to the macroeconomic development of end-use sectors which is supported by regional GDP and population growth.

demand_outlook.claim: The CPP films industry is projected to expand at a robust rate due to rising packaging requirements across sectors.
demand_outlook.quote: With the rising requirement for packaging across sectors, with traditional businesses preferring to package products, and the retail and e-commerce growing rapidly, the CPP films industry is projected to expand at a robust rate.

demand_outlook.claim: Revenue and net profit declined during the year due to lower demand for acrylic fibre and negative returns in the CPP segment caused by falling selling prices.
demand_outlook.quote: Revenue and Net profit during the year declined due to lower demand of acrylic fibre and negative return on CPP Segment caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

demand_outlook.claim: Sales and production declined due to lower demand, but improved in the last quarter of FY 2023-24 due to better market sentiments.
demand_outlook.quote: During the year, the sale and production was declined due to lower demand but in the last quarter of FY 2023-24, it was improved due to better sentiments in the market and it is expected to improve in the coming years.

demand_outlook.claim: Acrylic Fibre consumption improved during the year as COVID-19 concerns subsided.
demand_outlook.quote: During the year under review, Acrylic Fibre consumption has been improved as COVID-19 related concerns were subsided.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for Acrylic Fibre increased, with production reaching 36,425 MT and sales reaching 35,260 MT.
demand_outlook.quote: Demand of Acrylic Fibre has risen and the Company’s production and sales of Acrylic Fibre was 36,425 MT and 35,260 MT respectively as compared to production of 29,652 MT and sales of 30,918 MT during the previous year.

demand_outlook.claim: The packaging industry is growing rapidly due to rising packaging demand, expanding retail, and e-commerce growth.
demand_outlook.quote: With the rising requirement for packaging across sectors, with traditional businesses preferring to package products, and the retail and e-commerce growing rapidly, the industry is growing at a robust pace.

capex_expansion.claim: The company commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant and began commercial production in March 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based Ethanol Plant and commenced commercial production in March, 2025.

capex_expansion.claim: The total project cost for the ethanol plant was initially assessed at Rs. 167 Crore excluding working capital margin, but experienced cost overruns due to civil work.
capex_expansion.quote: The total project cost was assessed Rs. 167 Crore (excluding working capital margin) but the project was overrun due to Civil work.

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent approximately Rs. 188 Crore on the ethanol project, financed via Rs. 104 Crore in term loans and the remainder from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: Company has spent around Rs. 188 Crore so far which includes Rs. 104 Crore of Term Loan and Balance amount out of internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: A 750 KW solar power system has been installed by the company.
capex_expansion.quote: Solar Power System of 750 KW has been installed.

capex_expansion.claim: The Board approved setting up an Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD.
capex_expansion.quote: Board of Directors, at its meeting held on 18th May, 2022, had accorded its approval to the Company to set-up Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD to align with GOI’s Ethanol Blending Programme (E20), subject to clearance and approvals from the concerned statutory authorities.

capex_expansion.claim: The total project cost for the Ethanol Project is Rs. 167.58 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The total Project cost is Rs. 167.58 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Indian Bank sanctioned a term loan of Rs. 108 crores, with the remaining Rs. 59.58 crores to be met from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: Indian Bank had sanctioned Term Loan of Rs. 108 Crores and as per stipulations of sanction letter, the remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 would be met out of the Company’s internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has already spent around Rs. 92.17 crore on the project, including Rs. 44.08 crore of the term loan and the balance from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: However, the Company has already spent around Rs. 92.17 Crore so far which includes Rs. 44.08 Crores of Term Loan and balance amount out of internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: Civil work is ongoing at the site and major orders for plant and machinery have been placed.
capex_expansion.quote: Civil work is going on at the site and major order for Plant & Machinery has been placed.

capex_expansion.claim: The Board approved setting up a 150 KLPD Ethanol Project to align with the Government of India's E20 blending program.
capex_expansion.quote: Further, the Company is looking forward to diversify its business in Ethanol Product and accordingly, the Board of Directors, at its meeting held on May 18, 2022, accorded its approval to the Company to set-up Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD to align with GOI’s Ethanol Blending Programme (E20), subject to clearance and approvals from the concerned statutory authorities.

margins_costs.claim: Global consumption of acrylic fibre is impacted by input price volatility across raw materials, energy, and coal.
margins_costs.quote: Global Acrylic Fibre consumption is impacted due to volatility in prices of raw material, energy, coal and other key inputs.

margins_costs.claim: USD vs. INR foreign exchange fluctuations impact margins as the company relies on imports.
margins_costs.quote: Additionally, since the Company is dependent upon imports, the fluctuation in foreign exchange i.e. USD vs. INR has also a bearing on the margin of the Company.

margins_costs.claim: CPP segment losses decreased during the year owing to higher realization and reduced overhead costs.
margins_costs.quote: During the year under review, loss of CPP has been declined due to better realization and reduction in overheads.

margins_costs.claim: Cost optimization measures through alternate sourcing, standardization, and process improvements yielded significant savings.
margins_costs.quote: Various cost optimisation driven by way of alternate sourcing, standardization, process improvements and operational efficiency improvements has led significant savings.

margins_costs.claim: Operating profit margin, net profit margin, and return on net worth declined due to a relatively high cost of production compared to the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: Operating Profit Margin, Net Profit Margin and Return on Net Worth are declined as cost of production was relatively high as compared to previous year.

margins_costs.claim: The raw materials used to produce the company's products are derived from crude.
margins_costs.quote: The raw material to produce the Company’s products is crude derived.

margins_costs.claim: Crude prices remained volatile during the year under review due to conflicts in the Israel-Hamas War and Russia-Ukraine War.
margins_costs.quote: The fluctuation in crude affects the raw material prices to some extent and during the year under the review, the crude prices remained volatile due to conflict in Israel-Hamas War & Russia-Ukraine War.

margins_costs.claim: Net profit declined due to negative returns in the CPP Film segment caused by falling selling prices and excessive market capacity.
margins_costs.quote: Net profit during the year declined due to negative return on CPP Segment caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

margins_costs.claim: Raw material costs were affected by volatile and rising crude oil prices resulting from the Russia-Ukraine War.
margins_costs.quote: The fluctuation in crude affects the raw material prices to some extent and during the year under the review, the crude prices remained volatile and witnessed a continued rise due to Russia-Ukraine War.

orders_capacity.claim: The annual production capacity for acrylic products stands at 42,000 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: The production capacity to produce Acrylic products of the Company is 42,000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: In FY 2024-25, the company recorded acrylic fibre production of 35,198 MT and sales of 33,850 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the Company has recorded production of 35,198 MT and Sale of 33,850 MT, as against production of 31,534 MT and Sale of 31,685 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's CPP film manufacturing capacity is 10,000 MT per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: The Company’s production capacity to produce CPP film is 10000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: CPP film production and sales were 6,343 MT and 6,409 MT respectively in FY 2024-25.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film was 6,343 MT and 6,409 MT respectively as against production of 6,463 MT and sale of 6,476 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: During FY 2024-25, ethanol production was 790 KL and sales reached 440 KL.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of Ethanol was 790 KL and 440 KL respectively.

orders_capacity.claim: During the year under review, the company recorded acrylic production of 31,534 MT and sales of 31,685 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the Company has recorded production of 31,534 MT and Sale of 31,685 MT, as against production of 36,425 MT and Sale of 35,260 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film was 6,463 MT and 6,476 MT respectively.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film was 6,463 MT and 6,476 MT respectively as against production of 7,663 MT and sale of 7,640 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's installed production capacity for Acrylic products stands at 45,000 MT PA.
orders_capacity.quote: The production capacity to produce Acrylic products of the Company is 45,000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: The installed production capacity for CPP film is 10,000 MT PA.
orders_capacity.quote: The production capacity to produce CPP film is 10000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: CPP film production and sales increased to 7,663 MT and 7,640 MT respectively during FY 2022-23.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film increased to 7,663 MT and 7,640 MT respectively as against production of 6,348 MT and sale of 6,210 MT respectively during the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board of Directors decided against recommending a dividend for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year under review the Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2024-25.

capital_allocation.claim: The company chose not to transfer any funds to the General Reserve for the year ended March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors of your company, has decided not to transfer any amount to the General Reserve for the year ended 31st March, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The ethanol project capital outlay of Rs. 188 Crore included Rs. 104 Crore in term loans, with the remaining balance funded via internal accruals.
capital_allocation.quote: Company has spent around Rs. 188 Crore so far which includes Rs. 104 Crore of Term Loan and Balance amount out of internal accruals.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2023-24 as internal accruals are being utilized to set up the Ethanol Plant.
capital_allocation.quote: As the Company’s internal accruals is being utilized to set-up Ethanol Plant, the Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided not to transfer any amount to the reserves for the year under review.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors of your company, has decided not to transfer any amount to the Reserves for the year under review.

capital_allocation.claim: The company did not provide any loans, securities, or guarantees under Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013 during the year under review.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year under review, the Company has not given any loan or provided any security or guarantee in terms of Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided not to recommend a dividend for the year in order to plough back earnings.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors decided to plough back the earnings to strengthen the financials of the Company and not to recommend dividend for the year under review.

risks_headwinds.claim: Crude oil price volatility driven by ongoing international conflicts impacted raw material costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: The fluctuation in crude affects the raw material prices to some extent and during the year under the review, the crude prices remained volatile due to conflict in Israel-Hamas War & Russia-Ukraine War.

risks_headwinds.claim: Ethanol prices are fixed by Oil Marketing Companies, leaving the company with no control over pricing.
risks_headwinds.quote: The prices of ethanol products are determined by Oil Marketing Companies (“OMC”) and the Company has no control on the prices.

risks_headwinds.claim: The absence of increases in Minimum Selling Price adjustments presents direct threats to forward planning and return on invested capital.
risks_headwinds.quote: Additionally, the continued absence of non-increase in Minimum Selling Price adjustments pose direct threats to forward planning, capacity utilisation, and return on invested capital

risks_headwinds.claim: The company faces challenges such as volatility in crude and raw material prices, dumping of acrylic fibre by China, Thailand, and Belarus, and foreign exchange fluctuations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Despite various challenges such as volatility in crude prices and raw material prices, dumping of acrylic fibre by China, Thailand and Belarus, foreign exchange fluctuations, the Company is focused on improvement in its revenue and net profit.

risks_headwinds.claim: Key risks include geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, subdued global economic conditions, changes in government policies, trade sanctions, intense competition, regulatory changes, and cyber security threats.
risks_headwinds.quote: Geo-political tensions including supply chain disruption, subdued global economic conditions, changes in government policies and trade sanctions and restrictions, intense competition from local and global players, regulatory changes and cyber security threats are key risks which expose the Company to potential challenges and uncertainties.

risks_headwinds.claim: Since the company depends on imported raw materials, movements in the USD and increases in crude oil prices due to ongoing wars may affect margins.
risks_headwinds.quote: Further, since the Company is dependent upon imported raw materials, movement in USD and increase in crude oil prices due to ongoing Israel-Hamas war and Russia-Ukraine war may affect the margin.

risks_headwinds.claim: The global economy is likely to be affected by inflation, high energy costs, logistics issues, and international trade costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: Global economy is likely to be hit by inflation, continuing high energy cost, logistics issues and costs in international trade.

risks_headwinds.claim: Tightening of monetary policies by central banks to curb inflation may impact consumption in the Acrylic Fiber and CPP Films industries.
risks_headwinds.quote: Tightening of monetary policies by Central banks to curb inflation may have necessary impact which will impact consumption in general including Acrylic Fiber & CPP Films Industry.

risks_headwinds.claim: Operations faced challenges from volatile crude prices, high raw material costs, dumping of acrylic fibre, and foreign exchange fluctuations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Despite various challenges such as volatility in crude prices and abnormal rise in raw material prices, dumping of acrylic fibre by Turkey, China, Thailand and Belarus, foreign exchange fluctuations, the Company is focused on improvement in its growth and in a position to achieve a better turnover as compared to previous year.

risks_headwinds.claim: The global economy faces headwinds from elevated energy costs, logistics challenges, and international trade expenses.
risks_headwinds.quote: Global economy is likely to be hit by continuing high energy cost, logistics issues and costs in international trade.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to commence commercial production of its grain-based Ethanol Project by September 2024.
management_commitments.quote: Further, the Company has already initiated steps to establish grain based Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD and it is expected to commence commercial production of Ethanol by September, 2024.

management_commitments.claim: The company is continuously exploring new markets and increasing exports.
management_commitments.quote: The Company is continuously exploring new markets and increasing exports.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to diversify its business by establishing a 150 KLPD Ethanol Project adjoining its existing unit in Thakurdwara.
management_commitments.quote: Further, the Company is looking forward to diversify its business in Ethanol Product and accordingly, the Board of Directors, at its meeting held on May 18, 2022, accorded its approval to the Company to set-up Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD to align with GOI’s Ethanol Blending Programme (E20), subject to clearance and approvals from the concerned statutory authorities.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
